transcript.text: Our Dyson (one of the V ones, purple bits) keeps cutting out after about 5-10 seconds. Not every time - some days it does a whole room fine. It's maybe 5 years old. Already cleaned the filter and checked for blockages. Battery or something else?

That intermittent cutting out after just a few seconds is very typical of either the battery protection kicking in or a thermal cut-out tripping. We need to narrow down which one it is. First, was it on Boost/Max mode? Those modes drain a 5-year-old battery extremely fast and can trigger a low-battery shutdown quickly. If it was on Normal mode, please ensure it has been left charging fully (the light should show solid green or full charge) before testing again. Second, when you cleaned the filter, did you wash it in cold water and leave it to dry for at least 24 hours? Even slightly damp filters can cause the motor to overheat rapidly and cut out. If it was just vacuumed or not fully dry, that could be the culprit. Please let me know: 1) Was it on Boost mode? 2) Did you wash and fully dry the filter (24 hours), or just rinse/clean it?

On Max it nearly always stops within a few seconds, on normal it's less often. Filter was washed and left to dry 48 hours, so that's not it. Also my lights go blue, not green, and it shows full blue lights after charging.

Since the filter is clean and dry, and blockages are cleared, we can rule out overheating from airflow restriction. The fact that it cuts out almost immediately on Max mode but lasts longer on Normal points to the battery struggling under load or the protection circuit cutting in due to a voltage drop. On Dyson V-series models, blue lights indicate charging status (solid usually means fully charged). However, after 5 years, batteries often lose capacity. A degraded battery might show 'full' but collapse instantly when Max mode demands high current, triggering a safety cut-out. Before assuming the battery is dead, let's rule out a charging issue:
1. Ensure the charger is plugged into a working wall socket (not just the dock).
2. Wipe the metal contacts on the vacuum body and the charger dock with a dry cloth to ensure good connection.
3. Leave it charging for at least 3-4 hours even if the light goes solid sooner, then try Normal mode again. Does it still cut out after this full charge cycle?

Charger light comes on and the plug goes in properly. It's actually left on the charger permanently, so it's always fully charged. It's usually fine straight off the charger and worse once the battery's partly used. I haven't wiped the contacts, but I can. The battery isn't swollen or hot. Is it worth the £60+ for a new battery?

Given the age (5 years) and the specific symptom—working fine on Normal but cutting out almost instantly on Max—the most likely cause is a degraded battery. After 5 years of use, lithium-ion batteries lose capacity and develop higher internal resistance. This means they can show 'full' when idle or on low power, but the voltage collapses under the high current demand of Max mode, triggering the safety cut-out. Sometimes oxidation builds up, causing the battery to not actually charge fully despite the light showing solid blue. If it still cuts out after wiping the contacts and doing a fresh 3-4 hour charge, then the battery is probably the culprit. Is it worth replacing? Yes, if you plan to keep using it for more than another year or two. A new battery restores full runtime and power on Max mode. If you are happy with Normal mode only and don't mind the shorter run times, you could continue as is, but be aware the battery may eventually fail completely.
